data.description: Feature: Full-text search (SQLite FTS) — WL-0MKRPG61W1NKGY78 Brief summary - Add an FTS5-backed full-text search index and a `worklog search` CLI so contributors can run fast, ranked queries (title, description, comments, tags) with immediate index visibility after writes. Problem statement - Developers and maintainers need fast, relevant full-text search over work items (title, description, comments, tags) so they can find and triage issues reliably at scale. Current listing and filtering are limited and do not support relevance ranking, snippets, or fast text queries. Users - Repository contributors and maintainers who search work items to triage, plan, and debug. Example user stories: - As a contributor, I want to run `worklog search "database corruption"` and see the most relevant items (with snippets) so I can find prior discussions quickly. - As a release engineer, I want to filter search results by `--status open --tags cli` and export JSON for automation so I can programmatically build reports. - As a maintainer, I want the search index to reflect writes immediately so newly created/updated items are discoverable in the next command. Chosen approach (capture fidelity) - SQLite FTS5 is the target engine (user confirmed). Index all text fields plus tags (title, description, comments, tags, other text fields). CLI defaults: human-friendly output with snippets and filters; `--json` for machine consumption. Success criteria - Search returns ranked, relevant results for common queries (top-10 relevance) with snippet highlights matching query terms. - Index updates synchronously on write: create/update/delete operations are visible to subsequent searches within 1 second. - CLI usability: `worklog search ` supports `--status`, `--parent`, `--tags`, `--json`, `--limit` and returns human-friendly output by default; `--json` returns structured results. - Performance: median query latency <100ms on datasets up to ~5,000 items in CI/dev environment; include a small benchmark job in CI. - Tests & CI: unit tests for indexing/querying, integration fixtures covering index correctness and consistency across create/update/delete, and a perf benchmark. Constraints - Requires SQLite with FTS5 enabled; the CLI must detect and fail fast with a clear message if FTS5 is unavailable. - Keep index consistent with the canonical store (SQLite DB or `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` import flow). Prefer DB-backed storage and transactional updates. - Implement synchronous updates with minimal write latency (FTS virtual table + triggers or application-managed transactions that update FTS in the same transaction). Existing state & traceability - Work item: WL-0MKRPG61W1NKGY78 (Feature: Full-text search). - Parent epic: WL-0MKRJK13H1VCHLPZ — Epic: Add bd-equivalent workflow commands. - Related infra: WL-0MKRRZ2DN0898F / WL-0MKRSO1KD1NWWYBP — Persist Worklog DB across executions; these inform DB choice/lifecycle. - Source data: `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` — use for initial backfill and test fixtures. - Docs: update `CLI.md` with `worklog search` usage and examples. Desired change (high level) - Add FTS5 virtual table `worklog_fts` that indexes title, description, comment bodies, tags and other text fields; include per-document metadata (work item id, status, parentId) to support filtering and ranking. - Keep index in sync synchronously on write via triggers or application-managed transactions; provide `--rebuild-index` admin flag to backfill or rebuild. - Implement `worklog search` supporting: phrase queries, prefix search, bm25 ranking, snippet extraction, filters `--status/--parent/--tags`, `--limit`, and `--json` output. - Provide migration/bootstrap: create FTS table on first run and backfill from `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` or current DB. Example SQL (developer handoff) ``` -- Create a simple FTS5 table tying back to the canonical items table CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS worklog_fts USING fts5( title, description, comments, tags, itemId UNINDEXED, status UNINDEXED, parentId UNINDEXED, tokenize = 'porter' ); -- Example ranked query with snippet SELECT itemId, bm25(worklog_fts) AS rank, snippet(worklog_fts, '', '', '...', -1, 64) AS snippet FROM worklog_fts WHERE worklog_fts MATCH '"database corruption" OR database*' ORDER BY rank LIMIT 10; ``` Related work (links/ids) - WL-0MKRPG61W1NKGY78 — this item. - WL-0MKRJK13H1VCHLPZ — parent epic. - WL-0MKRRZ2DN0898F / WL-0MKRSO1KD1NWWYBP — DB persistence work (relevant). - `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` — backfill and fixtures. - `CLI.md` — update after implementation. Risks & mitigations - FTS5 unavailable in some SQLite builds — Mitigation: detect early, emit a clear error message and document runtime requirements; create a follow-up fallback task if adoption is required. - Noisy/irrelevant results — Mitigation: tune tokenization, add field weighting, provide examples in docs, and expose `--limit` and filter flags for deterministic results. - Index corruption or schema drift during upgrades — Mitigation: provide `--rebuild-index`, export/backups before migration, and include migration scripts in the PR. - Write latency on very large datasets — Mitigation: measure with CI benchmark; keep transactional updates fast; evaluate async updates as follow-up if necessary. Polish & handoff - Update `CLI.md` with usage examples and the SQL snippet above. Include a short dev guide in the PR describing bootstrap steps, `--rebuild-index`, and how to run the perf benchmark. - Final one-line headline for work item body: "FTS5-backed full-text search + `worklog search` CLI: fast, ranked queries over title, description, comments and tags with synchronous indexing." Suggested next steps (conservative) 1) Merge this intake draft into the work item description (after your approval). 2) Create a small spike branch: add FTS5 table + backfill script + prototype `worklog search --json` and run local perf tests. 3) If FTS5 is absent in some environments, open a follow-up work item to add an application-level fallback.
data.title: Full-text search

# Worklog doctor intake brief (WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6)

## Problem statement
Worklog lacks a reliable, non-destructive diagnostics command to evaluate the integrity and consistency of worklog data during regular use. We need `worklog doctor` to report integrity issues, apply safe workflow-alignment fixes, and interactively handle non-safe fixes without tying results to build/CI failure semantics.

## Users
- Maintainers and SREs who need to validate worklog data health during routine operations.
- Developers and agents who need clear diagnostics and guided remediation when issues are found.

### Example user stories
- As a maintainer, I want `worklog doctor` to summarize integrity problems and guide fixes so the worklog remains consistent during daily use.
- As a developer, I want `worklog doctor --fix` to apply safe workflow-alignment fixes automatically and prompt me on non-safe changes.

## Success criteria
- `worklog doctor` reports integrity findings for graph integrity and status/stage validation.
- Human output is an informative summary; `--json` outputs a single array of detailed findings.
- `--fix` applies safe fixes automatically and prompts interactively for non-safe fixes.
- Safe fixes are limited to workflow-alignment changes; non-safe fixes are never applied without user confirmation.
- The command is usable during regular operations and does not imply CI/build failure behavior.

## Suggested next step
Proceed to implementation planning for `worklog doctor` with `--fix` support, aligning graph integrity and status/stage validation checks to the documented rules and data stores.

## Constraints
- No `--fail-on` or build/CI failure semantics.
- No severity labels on findings.
- Fixing is interactive for non-safe changes.
- Operate on the canonical worklog datastore (DB) and existing JSONL exports.

## Existing state
- Work items and dependency edges are persisted in `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and the SQLite DB.
- Status/stage rules and known validation gaps are documented in `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md`.

## Desired change
- Implement `worklog doctor [--json] [--fix]`.
- Detect graph integrity issues (cycles, missing parents, dangling dependency edges, orphaned non-epic items, malformed/duplicate ids if format rules exist).
- Detect status/stage values that violate config-driven rules.
- Produce an informative human summary by default; `--json` emits a single array of detailed findings.
- When `--fix` is enabled:
  - Apply safe fixes automatically (workflow-alignment changes).
  - Prompt interactively for non-safe fixes (anything not easily reversible).
  - Report any declined non-safe fixes as remaining findings.

## Related work
- Doctor: detect missing dep references (WL-0ML4PH4EQ1XODFM0) — child item for dangling dependency checks.
- Doctor: validate status/stage values from config (WL-0MLE6WJUY0C5RRVX) — child item for status/stage validation.
- Add wl dep command (WL-0ML2VPUOT1IMU5US) — dependency edges and semantics.
data.title: wl doctor

Problem
- Worklog currently uses a Map-backed in-memory database (src/database.ts) and relies on importing/exporting .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl per CLI invocation (src/cli.ts) and at API server startup (src/index.ts).
- There is no persistent database process/state that survives between separate CLI runs, and the “source of truth”/refresh behavior is ad-hoc.
- We want a real persistent DB (on disk) so the database state exists independently of a single process, and a clear refresh rule: if the local JSONL file is newer than what the DB has, reload/refresh the DB from JSONL.
Goal
- Replace the “in-memory Map only” approach with a disk-backed database that persists between command executions.
- Ensure the DB automatically refreshes from .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl when that file is newer than the DB’s current state.
Proposed behavior
- On CLI start and API server start:
  - Open/connect to the persistent DB stored on disk (location configurable; default under .worklog/).
  - Determine staleness:
    - Compare JSONL mtime vs DB “last imported from JSONL” timestamp (or DB file mtime if that’s the chosen proxy).
  - If JSONL is newer:
    - Re-import from JSONL into the DB (rebuild items/comments).
    - Update DB metadata to record the import time + source file path + JSONL mtime/hash (so future comparisons are reliable).
- On writes (create/update/delete/comment ops):
  - Persist to DB immediately.
  - Decide and document the new “source of truth” model:
    - Option A: DB is source of truth; JSONL is an export artifact (write JSONL on demand or on a schedule).
    - Option B: Keep writing JSONL for Git workflows, but DB remains authoritative for runtime and only refreshes from JSONL when JSONL is newer (e.g., after a git pull).
Scope / tasks
- Add a persistent DB implementation (likely SQLite) and a small DB metadata table, e.g.:
  - meta(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT) with keys like lastJsonlImportMtimeMs, lastJsonlImportAt, schemaVersion.
- Refactor database layer:
  - Introduce an interface (e.g. WorklogStore) implemented by the new persistent DB.
  - Keep the current Map DB as a fallback/dev option if desired, but default to persistent.
- Update CLI (src/cli.ts):
  - Replace loadData()/saveData() logic with “open DB; maybe refresh from JSONL; operate on DB; optionally export JSONL”.
  - Ensure multi-project prefix behavior still works.
- Update API server startup (src/index.ts):
  - Same refresh logic on boot.
- Refresh logic details:
  - Use fs.statSync(jsonlPath).mtimeMs (or async equivalent).
  - Compare against stored DB metadata value; if JSONL missing, do nothing.
  - If DB is empty/uninitialized and JSONL exists, import.
- Add migration/versioning:
  - DB schema version stored in metadata; handle upgrades safely.
- Tests / acceptance checks
  - Running worklog create then a separate worklog list shows the created item without relying on in-process state.
  - If .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl is modified externally (simulate git pull), the next CLI/API startup refreshes DB and reflects the updated data.
  - If DB has newer data than JSONL, it does not overwrite DB (unless explicitly commanded); behavior is documented.
Acceptance criteria
- DB persists across separate CLI executions (verified by creating an item, exiting, re-running list/show).
- On startup (CLI + API), if .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl is newer than DB state, DB is refreshed from JSONL automatically.
- No data loss when switching from current JSONL-only workflow: existing .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl is imported into the new DB on first run.
- Clear documented “source of truth” and when JSONL is written/updated.
Notes / implementation preference
- SQLite is a good default (single file on disk, easy distribution, supports concurrency better than ad-hoc JSON).
- Keep .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl for Git-friendly sharing, but treat it as an import/export boundary rather than the primary store.
data.title: Persist Worklog DB across executions; refresh from JSONL when newer

Users should be able to download a release artifact, extract it, place it on their PATH, and run worklog without installing Node or running npm install. We’ll implement a per-platform “folder distribution” that bundles:
- a small worklog launcher (or worklog.exe)
- a Node.js runtime
- the compiled Worklog CLI (dist/)
- runtime dependencies, including the native better-sqlite3 addon for that platform
This is explicitly not a single-file executable; it’s a self-contained directory that can be put on PATH.
Goals
- worklog runs on a clean machine with no Node/npm installed.
- Distributions are produced for at least: linux-x64, darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, win-x64 (expand as needed).
- Release artifact layout is stable and documented.
- CLI behavior is unchanged (same commands/options/output).
Non-goals
- Single-file executable.
- Replacing better-sqlite3.
- Building from source on user machines.
Implementation plan
1) Choose packaging approach (recommended)
- Bundle Node runtime + app into a folder:
  - node (or node.exe)
  - worklog launcher script/binary that executes the bundled node:
    - linux/macos: ./node ./dist/cli.js "$@"
    - windows: worklog.cmd or worklog.exe shim calling node.exe dist\cli.js %*
  - dist/ output from tsc
  - node_modules/ containing production deps (incl. better-sqlite3 compiled binary)
2) Add packaging scripts
- Add npm run build (already exists) + new scripts such as:
  - npm run dist:prep to create a clean staging directory
  - npm run dist:bundle to copy dist/, package.json, and install production deps into staging
  - npm run dist:node:<platform> to download/extract the correct Node runtime into staging (or use a build action to fetch it)
  - npm run dist:archive to produce .tar.gz / .zip per platform
- Ensure we install prod-only deps into staging (no devDependencies).
3) Handle native module compatibility (better-sqlite3)
- Build artifacts must be produced on each target OS/arch (or use CI runners per platform) so better-sqlite3’s .node binary matches the target.
- Verify that the bundled node version matches the ABI expected by the built better-sqlite3 binary (i.e., build/install using the same Node major version you bundle).
4) Entrypoint and pathing
- Ensure the CLI entry works when executed from anywhere:
  - Use process.execPath / import.meta.url-relative paths so it finds dist/ and bundled resources regardless of current working directory.
- Confirm that .worklog/ data paths remain in the current project directory (unchanged).
5) Versioning and update UX
- Add worklog --version (already) and optionally a worklog version --json output for tooling (optional).
- Document upgrade procedure: replace the folder on PATH with a newer version.
6) CI build + GitHub releases
- Add GitHub Actions workflow:
  - Matrix: ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest (and macos for both x64/arm64 as appropriate)
  - Steps: checkout, install, build, stage folder, run smoke tests, archive, upload artifacts
  - On tag push: create GitHub Release and attach artifacts
7) Smoke tests (required)
- On each platform artifact in CI:
  - Extract artifact
  - Run ./worklog --help
  - Run ./worklog --version
  - Optionally run a minimal command that doesn’t require repo init (e.g., worklog status should error cleanly) to confirm runtime works.
8) Documentation
- Update README.md with:
  - Download links / artifact names
  - Install instructions per OS (PATH update examples)
  - Notes about per-platform downloads
  - Troubleshooting: macOS Gatekeeper/quarantine, Linux executable bit, Windows SmartScreen
Acceptance criteria
- A user can:
  - download the correct artifact for their OS/arch
  - extract it
  - add the extracted directory to PATH
  - run worklog --help successfully with no Node/npm installed
- CI produces and uploads artifacts for the supported platforms on every release tag.
- Artifacts include better-sqlite3 correctly (no missing native module errors).
Notes / risks
- macOS: may require signing/notarization for best UX; at minimum document Gatekeeper prompts.
- Windows: consider providing both worklog.cmd shim and (optional) an .exe shim.
- Size: bundling Node increases artifact size; this is expected for “no Node required”.
data.title: Ship Standalone “Folder Binary” Distribution (No npm install) for Worklog CLI

We need a `next` command that will evaluate the state of the database and suggest the next item that should be worked on. Initially this will be a simplistic algorithm as follows:

- Find in progress items.
- If there are none currently in progress find the item that is highest priority and oldest (created first).
- If there are in progress items walk down the tree of the highest priority / oldest item until you find all the leaf nodes that are not in progress
- Select the leaf node that is highest priority and oldest

When the result is presented, if we are not using --json then the user should offered the opportunity to copy the ID into the clipboard.

It should be possible to filter the results by --assignee.

It should be possible to provide a search term that will fuzzy match against title, description and comments (any item without the search term in one of these places will not be considered).

Note that later iterations will use more complex algorithms for identifying the next item.

data.description:
Summary
- Update the `wl next` selection logic to treat `updatedAt` (modification time) as a configurable signal (recency boost or penalty) and move from simple priority+createdAt tie-breaking to a multi-factor scoring function.

Why
- Current algorithm uses priority and creation time only (see `src/database.ts::selectHighestPriorityOldest`) which makes creation time the dominant tie-breaker. That causes recently-updated items to not be surfaced appropriately and encourages gaming by creating older stubs.
- Modification time (`updatedAt`) is a valuable signal: it can indicate recent discussion (should often be de-prioritized briefly) or recent activity requiring follow-up (should be surfaced). Making it configurable avoids hard assumptions.

Files of interest
- src/commands/next.ts
- src/database.ts

Proposed changes
1. Add a modular scoring function `computeScore(item, now, options)` that combines:
   - priority (primary)
   - due date proximity (if present)
   - blocked status (large negative if blocked)
   - assignee match (boost if assigned to current user)
   - effort (smaller items encouraged)
   - age (createdAt; small boost to older items to avoid starvation)
   - updatedAt recency: configurable as either a penalty for very recent updates or a boost for recent updates (policy option)
2. Replace `selectHighestPriorityOldest` and related selection points with `selectByScore(items, opts)` using the scoring function. Keep a stable tie-breaker (createdAt then id).
3. Add CLI flags to `wl next`:
   - `--recency-policy <prefer|avoid|ignore>` (default: avoid) to choose how updatedAt affects score
   - optional weight flags (advanced) or use config file to tune weights
4. Add unit tests covering:
   - prefer older items when priorities equal
   - penalize items edited in the last X hours (avoid)
   - prefer recently-updated items when policy=prefer
   - behavior with blocked/critical items remains unchanged
5. Document the behavior change in CLI.md and RELEASE notes.

Acceptance criteria
- `wl next` uses the scoring function and yields deterministic, explainable selection reasons
- New CLI flag `--recency-policy` works and is documented
- Tests added for core scoring behaviors

Notes
- This is non-destructive; default behavior should match existing behavior closely (use small age boost and a modest recent-update penalty by default).
- I will implement the change and include tests if you want; please confirm whether default `recency-policy` should be `avoid` (recommended) or `prefer`.
data.title: Improve 'wl next' selection algorithm to include modification time and scoring

Summary

Provide a new UI for updating a work-item's stage (and related fields) inspired by the existing close UI. The initial scope is to allow changing the stage of an item, but the component must be designed to grow to support other quick edits (status, comments, assignees, tags) so the keyboard shortcut and UX are generic. Suggest the primary keyboard shortcut be `U` (for Update) and follow existing patterns used by the close UI.

User stories

- As a Producer or Agent, I want to quickly change an item's stage (eg. idea -> in_progress -> review) without opening a full edit page so I can triage and advance work more efficiently.
- As a keyboard-focused user, I want a single, discoverable shortcut (`U`) to open a compact, accessible modal/popover to make quick changes.
- As a developer, I want a reusable component that can later include status changes, adding comments, and other small edits without a large refactor.

Expected behavior

- Pressing `U` when a work-item is focused opens the Update UI (modal or popover) similar in layout and affordances to the close UI.
- The UI shows the current stage, a list/dropdown of available stages (respecting permissions), and a Confirm/Cancel action.
- Choosing a new stage and confirming updates the work-item and closes the UI. The change should be optimistic or show a short saving state and surface errors.
- The UI should be accessible (keyboard navigable, ARIA roles) and mobile-friendly.

Suggested implementation approach

- Reuse the close UI component patterns: same modal/popover wrapper, header, action layout, and keyboard handling where appropriate.
- Implement a generic `QuickEdit` or `UpdatePanel` component with a small API that supports multiple field types (stage, status, inline comment). Initially only implement the `stage` field.
- Wire the `U` keyboard shortcut to open the component when a work-item row/card is focused. Keep the shortcut registration centralized so future quick-actions can share shortcuts.
- Ensure server API call is the same as used by the full edit flow (reuse existing update endpoint) and that the frontend updates local store/cache appropriately.
- Add unit and integration tests for the component and keyboard shortcut behavior.

Acceptance criteria

1. New work item (feature) exists in Worklog for this task.
2. Pressing `U` opens an Update UI for the focused item.
3. The UI allows selecting a new stage and confirms the change via the existing update API.
4. The UI handles success and error states and is keyboard accessible.
5. Code is implemented as a reusable component that can be extended to other quick edits.
6. Tests cover the main flows and the keyboard shortcut.

Notes / Risks / Dependencies

- Depends on existing close UI patterns; developer should review `Close` UI implementation for consistency.
- Permission checks: only allow stage changes for users with the required permissions; surface a message if not allowed.
- Decide whether `U` conflicts with other shortcuts; coordinate with global shortcut registry.

Suggested priority: medium
data.title: Add 'Update' UI to change work-item stage (shortcut: U)

Summary:
Replace the current Tab-based focus advancement in the affected component with Alt+Right Arrow. This work item updates the intended keyboard shortcut and documents expected behaviour and acceptance criteria.

Context:
The component currently advances focus with the Tab key. We want to change the shortcut to Alt+Right Arrow to avoid interfering with native Tab behaviour (sequential focus navigation) and to provide a more explicit, single-key modifier shortcut for this specific action.

User Stories:
- As a keyboard user, I can press Alt+Right Arrow to move the component's internal focus to the next interactive element without changing global Tab order.
- As a user relying on standard Tab navigation, pressing Tab should retain default browser/system behaviour and not trigger the component-specific focus advance.

Expected behaviour:
- Pressing Alt+Right Arrow moves focus to the next logical interactive element within the component.
- Pressing Alt+Left Arrow (if applicable) should move focus to the previous element (if this pattern exists today; if not, consider whether to implement a symmetric shortcut).
- Tab and Shift+Tab continue to perform standard sequential focus navigation and do not trigger the component-specific action.
- Shortcut should be documented in the component's accessibility notes and any visible hints/tooltips where applicable.

Steps to reproduce (before change):
1. Open the component UI that currently uses Tab to advance internal focus.
2. Press Tab and observe the component-specific focus change.

Suggested implementation approach:
- Update the component's keyboard handler to listen for Alt+Right Arrow (e.g. check for `event.altKey && event.key === 'ArrowRight'`) and call the existing focus-advance logic.
- Ensure the handler prevents default only when the Alt+Right combination is used; do not prevent default on plain Tab/Shift+Tab.
- Add unit and keyboard-integration tests to verify behaviour (Alt+Right advances focus; Tab does not trigger the component-specific advance).
- Update documentation and release notes to call out the new shortcut.

Acceptance criteria:
- The work item demonstrates a code change (or spec change) where Alt+Right Arrow is used to advance focus.
- Tests validating the new behaviour are added or updated.
- Documentation (component docs or accessibility notes) is updated to reference Alt+Right Arrow.
- No regression in standard Tab/Shift+Tab focus behaviour.

Notes:
- If other shortcuts use Alt+Right Arrow in the app, evaluate conflicts and adjust accordingly.
- Consider whether Alt+Left Arrow should be implemented for backward navigation and whether it should be part of this ticket or a follow-up.

- As a contributor I can sort work items deterministically so the top of the list is the most important work to do next.
- As a producer I can set and persist the ordering of items to reflect priorities that are not captured by the `priority` field alone.

Expected behaviour:

data.description:
Implement real-time progress feedback for OpenCode interactions in the TUI by displaying current activity status and using visual indicators.

## Context

The TUI currently shows basic 'waiting' indicator in prompt label when OpenCode is processing. This work item enhances that to provide richer, real-time feedback about what OpenCode is doing.

Related Work Items:
- Parent: WL-0MKXJETY41FOERO2 (Epic: Platform - TUI)
- Related: WL-0MKW7SLB30BFCL5O (Epic: Opencode server + interactive 'O' pane) - completed
- Discovered-from: Recent commit 1826786 (blocking duplicate prompts)

Related Files:
- src/commands/tui.ts (lines ~973-1270: SSE event handling in connectToSSE function)
- docs/opencode-tui.md (TUI documentation)

## Problem

Users cannot see what OpenCode is currently doing when processing requests. The only feedback is a generic '(waiting...)' label. This creates uncertainty about whether OpenCode is thinking, reading files, writing code, or stuck.

## Solution

Enhance progress feedback using OpenCode's SSE event stream:

### 1. Response Pane Header Progress (Moderate Detail)
Display current activity in the response pane's title/header area:
- Update on activity change only (not every text chunk)
- Show moderate detail: 'Thinking...', 'Using tool: read', 'Writing files', 'Running command'
- Clear when operation completes

### 2. Prompt Label Spinner
Add animated Braille dots spinner after 'waiting' text:
- Pattern: ⠋ ⠙ ⠹ ⠸ ⠼ ⠴ ⠦ ⠧ ⠇ ⠏
- Shows during any processing activity
- Stops and clears when ready

### 3. Inline Messages (Detailed, Selective)
Insert detailed messages into response stream for:
- File operations: '[Writing: src/file.ts]', '[Editing: package.json]', '[Deleted: temp.js]'
- Questions/input requests: Already handled, ensure formatting consistency

## Event Types to Handle

Based on OpenCode SSE stream analysis:

### session.status (Primary State Indicator)
- status.type: 'busy' → Show spinner + activity
- status.type: 'idle' → Clear progress, stop spinner

Example events:
```json
{"type": "session.status", "properties": {"sessionId": "abc123", "status": {"type": "busy"}}}
{"type": "session.status", "properties": {"sessionId": "abc123", "status": {"type": "idle"}}}
{"type": "session.status", "properties": {"sessionId": "abc123", "status": {"type": "busy", "activity": "thinking"}}}
```

### message.part.updated (Activity Details)
- part.type: 'text' → Header: 'Writing response...'
- part.type: 'tool-use' + tool.name → Header: 'Using tool: {name}', Inline: '[Using {name}: {description}]' (for file ops only)
- part.type: 'tool-result' → Header: 'Processing result...', Inline: Show file ops results
- part.type: 'step-start' → Header: Show step description

Example events:
```json
{"type": "message.part.updated", "properties": {"part": {"type": "text", "text": "Let me help...", "messageID": "m1"}}}
{"type": "message.part.updated", "properties": {"part": {"type": "tool-use", "tool": {"name": "read", "description": "Reading file.ts"}, "messageID": "m1"}}}
{"type": "message.part.updated", "properties": {"part": {"type": "tool-use", "tool": {"name": "write", "description": "Writing src/test.ts"}, "messageID": "m1"}}}
{"type": "message.part.updated", "properties": {"part": {"type": "tool-result", "content": "File written successfully", "messageID": "m1"}}}
```

### message.updated (Message Lifecycle)
- Track message completion via time.completed field
- Clear progress when assistant message completes

Example events:
```json
{"type": "message.updated", "properties": {"info": {"id": "m1", "role": "assistant", "time": {"started": 1234567890}}}}
{"type": "message.updated", "properties": {"info": {"id": "m1", "role": "assistant", "time": {"started": 1234567890, "completed": 1234567900}}}}
{"type": "message.updated", "properties": {"info": {"id": "m2", "role": "user", "time": {"started": 1234567880, "completed": 1234567881}}}}
```

### question.asked (Already Handled)
- Ensure inline message formatting is consistent
- Example already in code at line ~1154

## Implementation Approach

1. Add spinner animation to prompt label
   - Use setInterval for Braille dots animation
   - Start when isWaitingForResponse = true
   - Stop when isWaitingForResponse = false
   - Update label: 'OpenCode (waiting {spinner})' or 'OpenCode Prompt'

2. Add activity tracking in connectToSSE
   - Track current activity state (idle, thinking, using_tool, writing, etc.)
   - Add function to update response pane title/label based on activity
   - Update only when activity changes (debounce)

3. Enhance event handlers (lines ~1053-1253)
   - session.status: Update activity state, start/stop spinner
   - message.part.updated: Update activity based on part.type and tool.name
   - For write/edit/delete tools: append inline message to stream
   - message.updated: Check for completion, clear progress

4. Add cleanup on operation complete
   - Reset activity state to idle
   - Stop spinner animation
   - Clear response pane header progress
   - Restore default labels

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Response pane header shows current activity (thinking, using tool: X, writing, etc.)
- [x] Activity updates on state change only, not on every text chunk (smooth performance)
- [x] Prompt label shows animated Braille dots spinner during processing
- [x] Spinner stops when operation completes or errors
- [x] File operations (write, edit, delete) show inline messages with file names
- [x] Questions/input requests display with consistent inline formatting
- [ ] No UI flickering or performance degradation during high-frequency SSE events
- [x] Progress indicators clear properly when operation completes
- [ ] No regressions to existing features (autocomplete, input requests, streaming, etc.)
- [ ] Code follows existing TUI patterns and blessed.js conventions

## Testing

Manual testing:
1. Open TUI, press 'o' to open OpenCode
2. Send prompt: 'Read the package.json file and tell me the version'
   - Verify spinner appears in prompt label
   - Verify header shows 'Using tool: read'
   - Verify response streams correctly
   - Verify spinner stops when complete

3. Send prompt: 'Create a new file test.ts with a hello function'
   - Verify header shows 'Using tool: write'
   - Verify inline message: '[Writing: test.ts]'
   - Verify spinner animation is smooth
   - Verify everything clears when done

4. Send prompt while previous is processing
   - Verify blocked with toast message (existing feature)
   - Verify spinner continues for original request

5. Test with rapid streaming (long response)
   - Verify no flickering or performance issues
   - Verify header updates appropriately

## Updates
- Prompt spinner implemented in the OpenCode prompt label and clears on completion/errors.
- Default OpenCode port is now unset unless OPENCODE_SERVER_PORT is provided, allowing server auto-selection.

# Delegate to GitHub Coding Agent

Add a `wl github delegate <work-item-id>` subcommand that pushes a Worklog work item to GitHub (creating or updating the issue as needed) and assigns it to the GitHub Copilot Coding Agent (`copilot`), enabling one-command delegation of work to Copilot from the Worklog CLI.

## Problem Statement

There is no way to delegate a Worklog work item to GitHub Copilot Coding Agent from the CLI. Users must manually push the item to GitHub with `wl github push`, then navigate to the GitHub UI (or run separate `gh` commands) to assign the issue to Copilot. This multi-step process is error-prone and slow, especially when delegating multiple items.

## Users

- **Worklog CLI users** who want to offload implementation work to GitHub Copilot Coding Agent.
  - *As a developer, I want to delegate a work item to Copilot with a single command so that I can quickly hand off well-defined tasks without leaving my terminal.*
  - *As a team lead, I want the local Worklog state to reflect that an item has been delegated so that team dashboards and `wl in-progress` queries accurately show who is working on what.*

## Success Criteria

1. Running `wl github delegate <work-item-id>` pushes the work item to GitHub (smart sync: only if stale or not yet created) and assigns the resulting issue to the `copilot` GitHub user.
2. The local Worklog item is updated: status set to `in_progress`, assignee set to `@github-copilot` (or the appropriate local convention).
3. If the work item has a `do-not-delegate` tag, the command warns and exits unless `--force` is provided.
4. If the work item has children, the command warns about them and lets the user decide whether to proceed (delegates only the specified item by default).
5. The command supports both human-readable output (progress messages + GitHub issue URL) and `--json` output, consistent with other `wl github` subcommands.
6. If the GitHub assignment fails (e.g., `copilot` user not available on the repository), the command reports a clear error and does not update local Worklog state.

## Constraints

- The delegation target is hardcoded to the `copilot` GitHub user. No configurable target is needed at this time.
- Assignment is done via `gh issue edit --add-assignee copilot` using the existing `gh` CLI wrapper infrastructure in `src/github.ts`.
- Must reuse the existing `wl github push` sync logic (`upsertIssuesFromWorkItems` in `src/github-sync.ts`) rather than reimplementing push behavior.
- Must respect the existing incremental push pre-filter (`src/github-pre-filter.ts`) for the "smart sync" behavior.
- The command must be registered as a subcommand of the existing `wl github` command group in `src/commands/github.ts`.

## Existing State

- `wl github push` can push work items to GitHub issues (create/update), including labels, comments, and parent-child hierarchy.
- The `workItemToIssuePayload()` function in `src/github.ts` does **not** currently map the `assignee` field to the GitHub issue payload.
- The `do-not-delegate` tag exists as a local convention (toggle via `wl update --do-not-delegate` or TUI `D` key) but has no effect on GitHub operations.
- No `gh issue edit --add-assignee` calls exist anywhere in the codebase.
- The `gh` CLI wrapper (`runGh`, `runGhAsync`, etc.) in `src/github.ts` supports running arbitrary `gh` subcommands with rate-limit retry/backoff.

## Desired Change

- Add a `delegate` subcommand to the `wl github` command group.
- The command flow:
  1. Resolve the work item by ID.
  2. Check for `do-not-delegate` tag; warn and exit unless `--force`.
  3. Check for children; warn and let the user decide.
  4. Push the work item to GitHub using the existing sync logic (smart sync: skip if already up to date).
  5. Assign the GitHub issue to `copilot` via `gh issue edit <issue-number> --add-assignee copilot`.
  6. Update local Worklog state: set status to `in_progress` and assignee to `@github-copilot`.
  7. Output success message with GitHub issue URL (human) or structured result (JSON).
- Add a new `assignGithubIssue` (or similar) helper function to `src/github.ts` to wrap the `gh issue edit --add-assignee` call.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption: `copilot` user is available.** The target repository must have GitHub Copilot Coding Agent enabled and the `copilot` user must be assignable. If not, the `gh issue edit --add-assignee` call will fail. Mitigation: clear error message (covered by SC #6).
- **Assumption: `gh` CLI is authenticated.** The existing `gh` wrapper handles auth, but delegation requires write access to the repository. Mitigation: rely on existing `gh` auth error reporting.
- **Risk: scope creep toward generic delegation.** The current scope is Copilot-only; future requests may ask for configurable targets, batch delegation, or automatic Copilot session monitoring. Mitigation: record these as separate work items linked to this one rather than expanding scope.
- **Risk: children warning UX in non-interactive mode.** When running with `--json` or in a pipeline, interactive prompts ("delegate children too?") may not be appropriate. Mitigation: default to single-item-only in non-interactive mode; require explicit flag for recursive behavior if added later.
- **Assumption: smart sync reuses existing pre-filter.** The incremental push pre-filter compares timestamps to decide whether to push. If the pre-filter skips an item that has never been pushed, the delegate command must still create the GitHub issue. This should work since `upsertIssuesFromWorkItems` creates issues for items without a `githubIssueNumber`, but this path should be tested.

## Related work (automated report)

### Work items

- **Scheduler: output recommendation when delegation audit_only=true (WL-0MLI9B5T20UJXCG9)** [open] -- The scheduler's delegation subsystem decides which items to delegate and to whom. The new `wl github delegate` command will be the mechanism for acting on those recommendations when the target is Copilot. These two features are complementary: the scheduler recommends, delegate executes.

- **Do not auto-assign shortcut (WL-0MLHNPSGP0N397NX)** [completed] -- Introduced the `do-not-delegate` tag and the TUI `D` toggle. The delegate command must respect this tag (SC #3), so the tag's semantics and storage (in the `tags` array) are a direct dependency for the guard-rail logic.

- **Next Tasks Queue (WL-0MLI9QBK10K76WQZ)** [open] -- Defines a priority queue that the scheduler and agents use to select the next item to work on. Items promoted via this queue may be prime candidates for delegation to Copilot, making the queue a natural upstream for the delegate command in future automation flows.

### Repository files

- **`src/commands/github.ts`** -- Registers the `wl github push` and `wl github import` subcommands. The new `delegate` subcommand will be added here alongside them, following the same registration pattern and sharing the config/output infrastructure.

- **`src/github-sync.ts`** -- Contains `upsertIssuesFromWorkItems()`, the push engine that creates/updates GitHub issues. The delegate command will call this function for its smart-sync step rather than reimplementing push logic.

## Problem Statement
Status and stage labels (and their legal combinations) are currently hard-coded in the TUI, creating inconsistent formatting and a split source of truth across TUI and CLI. This work makes labels and compatibility config-driven so both TUI and CLI render and validate against one shared, repo-specific definition.

## Users
- Contributors and agents who update work items via TUI or CLI and need consistent labels and rules.

### Example user stories
- As a contributor, I want status/stage labels to be consistent and configurable so TUI/CLI use a single source of truth.

## Success Criteria
- Status and stage labels and compatibility rules are sourced from `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml`.
- TUI update dialog renders labels from config and validates status/stage compatibility using config rules.
- CLI `wl create` and `wl update` reject invalid status/stage combinations with a clear error listing valid options.
- CLI accepts kebab-case values that map to valid snake_case values, with a warning on conversion.
- No remaining hard-coded status/stage label or compatibility arrays in the TUI/CLI code path.

## Constraints
- No backward compatibility: remove hard-coded defaults; if config is missing required sections, fail with a clear error.
- Canonical values and labels use `snake_case`.
- Compatibility is defined in one direction in config (status -> allowed stages); derive the reverse mapping in code.
- If CLI inputs are kebab-case equivalents of valid values, accept with warning; otherwise reject with error.

Problem statement
-----------------
Add a lightweight command-palette UI to the opencode prompt triggered by '/'. It should discover commands from .opencode/command and ~/.config/opencode/command, support fuzzy filtering, keyboard navigation, and allow Space to insert the top match into the prompt and close the palette.

Users
-----
- Primary users: developers using the opencode CLI/TUI to run commands and compose prompts. Example user story: "As a developer, I want to press '/' and quickly insert a matching command into my prompt so I can avoid typing the full command and stay focused in the terminal."

Success criteria
----------------
- Pressing '/' opens a modal palette overlaying the prompt.
- Typing filters the list of commands with fuzzy matching; searches should return results within ~200ms for 1000 commands on a typical developer machine.
- Pressing Space inserts the top-selected command into the prompt and closes the palette.
- Commands are discovered from .opencode/command and ~/.config/opencode/command (if present) and merged without duplicates.
- Automated tests cover discovery, filtering, selection, and insertion behaviors.

Constraints
-----------
- Respect existing keybindings and do not override Escape or Enter behavior outside the palette context.
- Files under .opencode and user config directories are the only sources for commands; do not attempt network discovery.
- Keep UI changes minimal and compatible with the repository's existing TUI rendering libraries (e.g., blessed).

Existing state
--------------
- Worklog item WL-0MLBTG16W0QCTNM8 exists with title "Implement '/' command palette for opencode" and is currently in-stage idea and assigned to Map.
- Related epic: Opencode server + interactive 'O' pane (WL-0MKW7SLB30BFCL5O) is completed and provides context for TUI integration.
- There are existing dialog and input helper refactors (see related work items) that may simplify implementing the palette.

Desired change
--------------
- Implement a modal command palette UI triggered by '/'.
- Add a command discovery module that reads and parses command definitions from specified locations and exposes them to the palette.
- Implement fuzzy filtering and keyboard navigation, and wire Space to insert the selection into the active prompt.
- Unit and integration tests plus a small user-facing docs update.

Risks & assumptions
-------------------
- Risk: Keybinding conflicts with existing shortcuts could degrade UX. Mitigation: restrict palette to when focus is on prompt and provide an opt-out config flag. (assumption: prompt focus is detectable)
- Risk: Large command lists may slow filtering. Mitigation: add incremental indexing or debounce user input; measure performance. (assumption: typical list size < 5000)

- Hardcoded path or environment variable pointing to `~/.config/opencode` when resolving the wl data store.
- Incorrect handling of relative vs absolute paths when invoked from the internal interface.
- Use of a global configuration store without respecting the current project's working directory or repository context.

Problem statement
-----------------
When filters applied to the work items pane return no visible open items the pane shows an unhelpful blank list or generic text. Users need a clear, contextual empty-state message that explains why the list is empty and offers an action when closed items exist.

Users
-----
- Primary: Developers and producers using the TUI to find or triage work items.
- Secondary: Automation users and CI authors who scan the TUI output during debugging.

User stories
-----------
- As a developer, when my filters match no open items I want the pane to tell me whether closed items exist and how to view them so I don't assume there is nothing in the project.
- As an accessibility-minded user, I want the empty-state message to be announced by screen readers so I immediately understand the state without extra navigation.

Success criteria
----------------
- When openCount == 0 and closedCount == 0 the pane shows a prominent, centered message: "No items are available." and no list rows are rendered.
- When openCount == 0 and closedCount > 0 the pane shows: "Only closed items are available — click \"Closed\" (bottom right) to view them." and provides an inline CTA or visible pointer to the Closed control that toggles the closed view.
- Messages are localised and announced to screen readers (use ARIA live region or role="status").
- Provide a thin metrics hook or telemetry event (optional) so product can measure how often the empty-state appears (add TODO comment if metrics system is not obvious).
- Unit tests cover message selection logic and an integration test verifies the CTA toggles the closed view.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints
-----------
- Keep changes small and local to the TUI code (src/tui/*). Avoid wide refactors.
- Follow existing empty-state component patterns and i18n conventions in the repo.
- Keyboard accessible and screen-reader compatible (no visual-only affordances).

- Add i18n keys for the two messages and wire them into the existing i18n system.
- Add unit tests for the selection logic and an integration test for the CTA toggling closed items.

Introduce a file-based (flock) process-level mutex to serialize access to the JSONL data file so concurrent processes don't cause merge races or data corruption.

## Problem
Multiple CLI processes or the API server can simultaneously read/modify the shared worklog-data.jsonl file. The exportToJsonl() method in database.ts performs a read-merge-write cycle that is susceptible to TOCTOU races. refreshFromJsonlIfNewer() can interleave with exports from other processes. The sync command performs fetch-merge-import-export-push without any lock.

## User Story
As a developer using Worklog in a team environment, I want concurrent wl commands to safely serialize their access to the shared JSONL data file so that no data is lost or corrupted due to race conditions.

## Implementation Approach
- Create a new src/file-lock.ts module that implements file-based locking using Node.js fs.open with O_EXCL (advisory lock file)
- The lock file will be placed alongside the JSONL data file (e.g., worklog-data.jsonl.lock)
- Provide withFileLock(lockPath, fn) helper that acquires the lock, runs the callback, and releases it (with proper cleanup on error)
- Include retry logic with configurable timeout and backoff for waiting on a held lock
- Include stale lock detection (process ID recorded in lock file, checked on acquisition failure)
- Integrate locking into WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl() and WorklogDatabase.refreshFromJsonlIfNewer()
- Integrate locking into the sync, import, and export command handlers
- Write tests that simulate concurrent processes to validate serialization

## Acceptance Criteria
- A new src/file-lock.ts module exists with withFileLock() and related helpers
- Import/export/sync operations acquire the lock before running and release after
- Stale locks (from crashed processes) are detected and cleaned up
- Tests simulate concurrent processes to validate serialization
- All existing tests continue to pass
- The lock does not introduce noticeable latency for single-process usage

## Problem statement

The AMPA triage scheduler's audit comments currently contain the entire raw output of `opencode run "/audit <id>"`, which includes tool call logs, intermediate reasoning, and other noise alongside the actual audit summary. Additionally, the audit skill's acceptance criteria validation is shallow -- it relies primarily on work item descriptions and comments rather than performing a thorough code review. This makes audit comments both noisy and insufficiently rigorous for verifying whether work is actually complete.

## Users

- **Producers reviewing work items:** As a producer, I want audit comments on work items to contain only a clear, structured status report with code-validated acceptance criteria verdicts so I can quickly and confidently understand the true state of each item without sifting through tool call noise.
- **Agents consuming audit comments:** As an automated agent, I want audit comments to follow a predictable structure with per-criterion verdicts so I can reliably extract status information for downstream processing (e.g. cooldown detection, delegation decisions, auto-close evaluation).
- **Discord notification consumers:** As a team member receiving Discord notifications, I want the triage audit summary to be extracted from a well-structured report so the notification is concise and accurate.

## Success criteria

1. The audit skill (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`) produces output with clearly defined delimiter markers (`--- AUDIT REPORT START ---` / `--- AUDIT REPORT END ---`) around the final structured report.
2. The structured report between the markers contains these sections in markdown: **Summary**, **Acceptance Criteria Status**, **Children Status**, and **Recommendation** (where applicable).
3. For the parent work item, the audit skill performs a deep code review for each acceptance criterion: reading the actual implementation code, assessing correctness, completeness, and edge cases. Each criterion receives a verdict (met/unmet/partial) with a one-line evidence note referencing the relevant file and line number.
4. For each child work item, the audit skill performs the same deep code review of acceptance criteria as for the parent. Each child's acceptance criteria are individually validated against the codebase with per-criterion verdicts and file references.
5. The triage audit runner (`ampa/triage_audit.py`) extracts only the content between the delimiter markers and posts that as the WL comment (under the existing `# AMPA Audit Result` heading).
6. The Discord notification is updated to extract the Summary section from the structured report (between delimiters) rather than applying regex heuristics to the full raw output.
7. When a work item or child has no acceptance criteria defined, the audit report notes this explicitly (e.g. "No acceptance criteria defined") rather than silently skipping the item.
8. Unit tests cover the marker extraction logic (including edge cases: missing markers, malformed output, empty report). A lightweight integration test verifies end-to-end format from the audit skill through to the posted comment structure.

## Constraints

- **Short-term fix:** This is an incremental improvement to comment quality and audit rigor. The broader initiative to replace comment-based audits with a structured `audit` field on work items (WL-0MLDJ34RQ1ODWRY0) remains a separate, future effort.
- **Breaking change acceptable:** The triage runner does not need to handle the old unstructured format. Once the audit skill is updated, old-format output can be dropped.
- **Truncation default unchanged:** The existing `truncate_chars` default (65536) is retained. Structured reports are expected to be much shorter in practice but the safety limit remains.
- **Audit skill is an OpenCode skill:** Changes to the audit skill output format are made in `~/.config/opencode/skill/audit/SKILL.md`, which is an instruction file for the AI agent -- not executable code. The skill instructions must be updated to mandate the structured output format with delimiters and the deep code review approach.
- **Triage runner is AMPA Python code:** The extraction and comment-posting logic lives in `~/.config/opencode/ampa/triage_audit.py` (and the legacy path in `~/.config/opencode/ampa/scheduler.py`).
- **Code review depth is instruction-driven:** The depth of code review depends on the AI agent following the skill instructions. The instructions should be explicit about reading implementation files, checking function signatures, verifying test coverage, and assessing edge cases -- not just checking that files exist.

## Existing state

- The audit skill (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`) produces freeform markdown output with a `# Summary` section. It does not use delimiter markers and does not enforce a consistent structure for all sections.
- The current skill mentions validating acceptance criteria "where appropriate, code in the repository" but this is vague. In practice the agent often relies on descriptions and comments rather than performing actual code review.
- The skill does not instruct the agent to review children's acceptance criteria against code -- it only lists child items by title, id, status, and stage.
- The triage audit runner (`triage_audit.py`) posts the entire stdout+stderr of `opencode run "/audit <id>"` as a WL comment under `# AMPA Audit Result`. It uses a regex-based `_extract_summary()` function to find a `Summary` section for Discord, but this is fragile and operates on the full raw output.
- Discord notifications currently receive the regex-extracted summary or a fallback of `<work-id> -- <title> | exit=<code>`.

## Desired change

1. **Audit skill update:** Modify `skill/audit/SKILL.md` to instruct the AI agent to:
   - Wrap the final report in `--- AUDIT REPORT START ---` and `--- AUDIT REPORT END ---` delimiters.
   - Structure the report with markdown headings: `## Summary`, `## Acceptance Criteria Status`, `## Children Status`, `## Recommendation`.
   - For the parent work item's acceptance criteria: perform a deep code review by reading the actual implementation code, assessing correctness and completeness against each criterion. Report each criterion as met/unmet/partial with a one-line evidence note including `file_path:line_number`.
   - For each child work item: extract the child's acceptance criteria and perform the same deep code review. Report per-criterion verdicts with file references. Present children as subsections under `## Children Status` with their own acceptance criteria tables.
   - Keep the report concise and actionable despite the deeper analysis.

2. **Triage runner update:** Modify `triage_audit.py` to:
   - Extract content between the `--- AUDIT REPORT START ---` and `--- AUDIT REPORT END ---` markers from the raw `opencode run` output.
   - Post only the extracted report as the WL comment (still under the `# AMPA Audit Result` heading).
   - If markers are not found, fall back to posting the full output (defensive behavior) but log a warning.

3. **Discord extraction update:** Update the Discord summary extraction to:
   - Parse the structured report (between markers) and extract the `## Summary` section.
   - Use this instead of the current regex heuristic on raw output.

4. **Tests:**
   - Unit tests for the marker extraction function covering: happy path, missing start marker, missing end marker, empty content between markers, multiple marker pairs (take first).
   - Unit tests for the updated Discord summary extraction.
   - Lightweight integration test verifying the audit skill output format contains the expected markers and sections.

## Risks & assumptions

- **AI compliance:** The deep code review behavior is instruction-driven. The AI agent may not consistently follow the skill instructions, producing varying output quality or omitting markers. Mitigation: the triage runner falls back to posting the full output and logs a warning when markers are missing.
- **Token/context budget:** Deep code review of parent + all children may exceed the AI agent's context window for work items with many children or large codebases. Mitigation: the skill instructions should cap the review to a reasonable depth (e.g. direct children only, not recursive grandchildren) and note when truncation occurs.
- **Runtime increase:** Deep code review will increase the duration of each audit run compared to the current shallow approach. Mitigation: the existing `_audit_timeout` / `AMPA_AUDIT_OPENCODE_TIMEOUT` configuration bounds execution time.
- **Scope creep:** This work item covers structured output format + deep code review of acceptance criteria. Additional ideas (e.g. structured audit field, delegation recommendations, auto-close improvements) should be tracked as separate work items (WL-0MLDJ34RQ1ODWRY0, WL-0MLI9B5T20UJXCG9) rather than expanding scope here.
- **Assumption: acceptance criteria format.** The skill assumes acceptance criteria are in a markdown section starting with `## Acceptance Criteria` formatted as a list. Work items that use a different format may have criteria missed or misidentified.

## Related work

# Intake Brief: Migrate GitHub Sync Helpers to Async Pattern

## Problem Statement

The codebase contains both synchronous and asynchronous GitHub integration functions. The synchronous versions (`ensureGithubLabels`, `listGithubIssues`) block the event loop and can cause performance issues when called from async contexts. The goal is to migrate all callers to use the async versions and deprecate the synchronous functions.

## Users

- **Developers** working with GitHub integration code will benefit from non-blocking async operations
- **TUI and CLI components** that currently use synchronous functions will see improved responsiveness
- **Plugin authors** who interact with GitHub will have consistent async APIs to work with

### Example User Stories

- As a developer, I want to fetch GitHub issues without blocking the event loop so the TUI remains responsive
- As a plugin author, I want to use async helpers for label management to avoid blocking other operations
- As a maintainer, I want a single consistent async API surface for GitHub operations

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All label management functions have async versions available (already exist)
- [ ] All issue listing functions have async versions available (already exist)
- [ ] All callers in the codebase use async versions
- [ ] Synchronous versions marked deprecated with JSDoc `@deprecated`
- [ ] All existing tests pass with the async migration
- [ ] Unit tests added or updated for async migration paths (verify no coverage regression)
- [ ] Integration tests verify async behavior works correctly

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility**: Must maintain sync versions until all callers are migrated
- **GitHub API rate limits**: Async operations should respect rate limiting (already handled by throttler)
- **Error handling**: Async versions must maintain same error handling as sync versions
- **Test coverage**: Must not reduce existing test coverage during migration

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

- **Scope creep**: Adding new features during migration could delay completion
  - *Mitigation*: Record opportunities for additional features/refactorings as work items linked to the main item, rather than expanding the scope of the current item

- **Breaking changes**: Converting sync to async could break existing callers if not properly awaited
  - *Mitigation*: Add comprehensive error handling tests and verify all callers properly await async functions

- **Performance regressions**: Async operations might introduce unexpected overhead
  - *Mitigation*: Profile before and after migration to ensure no performance degradation

- **Incomplete migration**: Some callers might be missed during migration
  - *Mitigation*: Run grep search after migration to verify all callers use async versions

### Assumptions

- Async versions already exist and are fully functional (already implemented in `src/github.ts`)
- All callers can be migrated without API changes
- No external consumers depend on the synchronous API
- Error handling behavior is identical between sync and async versions

## Existing State

### Current Synchronous Functions

- `ensureGithubLabels(config, labels)` - Synchronous label creation helper
- `listGithubIssues(config, since?)` - Synchronous issue listing with pagination
- `ensureGithubLabelsOnce(config, labels)` - Internal sync cache helper (used by `updateGithubIssue`)

### Current Asynchronous Functions (Already Exist)

- `ensureGithubLabelsAsync(config, labels)` - Async label creation with cache
- `listGithubIssuesAsync(config, since?)` - Async issue listing with pagination
- `ensureGithubLabelsOnceAsync(config, labels)` - Internal async cache helper

### Callers (Based on Code Search - grep results)

- `src/github.ts:1172` - Uses `ensureGithubLabelsOnce` in `createGithubIssueAsync`
- `src/github.ts:1249, 1264` - Uses `ensureGithubLabelsOnceAsync` internally
- `src/github.ts:1410` - Uses `ensureGithubLabelsOnce` in `updateGithubIssue`

## Desired Change

1. **Migrate callers** to use async versions:
   - Update `github-sync.ts` to use `listGithubIssuesAsync`
   - Update `updateGithubIssue` to use `ensureGithubLabelsOnceAsync` where appropriate

2. **Deprecate synchronous versions**:
   - Add `@deprecated` JSDoc comments to sync functions
   - Add migration notes in function comments

3. **Verify async behavior**:
   - Ensure async functions are properly awaited in all callers
   - Test error handling paths
   - Verify rate limiting works correctly

## Related Work

- **Parent epic**: WL-0MLGAYUH614TDKC5 - Wire CLI to async GitHub sync
- **GitHub integration**: `src/github.ts` (lines 467-1425) - Core GitHub API helpers
- **GitHub sync**: `src/github-sync.ts` (line 726) - Sync operations between Worklog and GitHub

# Async list issues and repo helpers / central throttler — WL-0MLGBAPEO1QGMTGM

Problem statement
- GitHub-related async helpers are in place, but requests are coordinated only via per-function bounded concurrency (e.g., `WL_GITHUB_CONCURRENCY` in `src/github-sync.ts`). There is no central throttler/token-bucket to enforce global request rates and bursts across all async GitHub calls, which makes it harder to reason about and control overall API usage and to simulate rate-limit behavior in tests.

Users
- Engineers and automation that run `wl github push`, `wl github sync`, and other GitHub-backed sync flows; CI or agent-run automation performing bulk syncs; maintainers who need predictable, testable API usage.

Example user stories
- As an engineer running `wl github push`, I want requests to GitHub to be globally rate-limited so I avoid secondary-rate-limit/abuse responses during large syncs.
- As a maintainer, I want a central throttler utility with clear config (env or config.yaml) so I can tune behavior per-environment.

Success criteria
1) Implement a reusable token-bucket throttler utility and export a single shared instance for GitHub calls; default behaviour uses token-bucket refill.
2) Migrate all async GitHub call sites (github helpers and callers, including `src/github-sync.ts`) to use the throttler so concurrency/rate is enforced globally.
3) Add unit tests for the throttler (token-bucket semantics) and integration tests exercising `github-sync` under simulated load and rate-limit conditions.
4) Update repository docs to explain throttler behaviour and how to tune the env vars.

Constraints
- Must avoid changing GitHub API semantics; throttler only changes client-side scheduling.
- Keep implementation small, dependency-free (vanilla TS/JS), and testable offline (use injectable clocks/mocks for timing in unit tests).
- Backwards-compatible: keep honoring `WL_GITHUB_CONCURRENCY` where used, but prefer centralized throttler when available.

Existing state
- `src/github-sync.ts` already uses `Number(process.env.WL_GITHUB_CONCURRENCY || '6')` in two places to bound concurrency for upserts and hierarchy checks. Many async helpers exist in `src/github.ts` (async variants, create/update/get/list helpers). No central throttler file or tests for a throttler were found.

Desired change
- Add `src/github-throttler.ts` (or similar) implementing a token-bucket with optional concurrency cap; export a default/shared instance wired by `config` helpers or env vars. Replace local concurrency pools in `src/github-sync.ts` and update other async GH callers to use the centralized throttler API (e.g., `throttler.schedule(() => helperAsync(...))`). Add unit and integration tests and documentation updates.

Related work
- `src/github-sync.ts` — existing sync logic and current per-function concurrency usage (see `upsertConcurrency` & `concurrency`).

Clear persisted GitHub mapping fields and local push-state with backups to prevent cross-machine sync conflicts.

Back up .worklog, clear githubIssueId/githubIssueNumber/githubIssueUpdatedAt from the DB, clear comment githubCommentId/githubCommentUpdatedAt, remove local push-state files and logs, and remove GitHub fields from .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl. Backups created under .worklog.bak and .worklog/*.bak.

Users
-----
 - Repository maintainers and operators who run `wl sync` and `wl github push`. Example user story: "As an operator, I want to remove persistent GitHub mapping fields and local push-state so that stale mappings don't persist across machines or cause sync conflicts when syncing with GitHub."

Success criteria
----------------
- A documented backup of .worklog is created under .worklog.bak before any clearing occurs.
- All GitHub mapping fields (githubIssueId, githubIssueNumber, githubIssueUpdatedAt, githubCommentId, githubCommentUpdatedAt) are cleared from the runtime DB and from exported `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` without data loss (original values preserved in the backup).
- Local push-state files and associated logs are removed or migrated to the approved per-machine storage solution, and the system remains functional for `wl github push` on machines with and without prior local state.
- Relevant tests updated and passing locally: unit tests referencing `githubIssueId` updated where necessary and the full project test suite run locally with no regressions.
- All related documentation and code comments updated to reflect the new behaviour, including README and developer notes where appropriate.

Constraints
-----------
- Must create backups before any destructive changes. Backups should be accessible under `.worklog.bak` and `.worklog/*.bak`.
- Maintain compatibility with the ephemeral JSONL transport pattern (Phase 2 design). Changes to `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` must follow the project's JSONL semantics.
- Preserve machine-local push-state semantics where required; do not introduce cross-machine data loss for legitimate push-state that is per-machine.

Risks & assumptions
--------------------
- Risk: Clearing fields may break tests or external integrations that expect persisted GitHub mappings. Mitigation: run and update tests, and preserve original values in backups.
- Risk: Removing push-state files could cause unexpected duplicate pushes or missed pushes on machines that relied on local state. Mitigation: prefer migration to per-machine store (WL-0MLWTYH2H034D79E) or clearly document the behavioural change.
- Risk: JSONL export/import incompatibility with other tools that parse GitHub fields. Mitigation: follow Phase 2 ephemeral JSONL semantics and include migration notes in the backup and release notes.
- Assumption: Backups stored under `.worklog.bak` will be accessible to maintainers and retained long enough for rollback if needed.
- Scope-scope mitigation: Record any additional features or refactors discovered while implementing this task as separate work items linked to this item; do not expand scope of this task during implementation.

Existing state
--------------
- The repo currently persists GitHub mapping fields in both the DB and JSONL exports. `src/github-sync.ts`, `src/persistent-store.ts`, `src/jsonl.ts`, and `src/github-push-state.ts` are primary touchpoints. Several tests and work items rely on seeded mapping fields.

Desired change
--------------
- Implement a safe clear-and-backup operation that: (1) creates a timestamped backup of `.worklog` and any JSONL exports, (2) clears mapping fields in the DB, (3) removes GitHub fields from `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl`, and (4) removes or migrates local push-state files/logs to the approved per-machine store.

If the work item is marked as in_review then an audit is triggered ('opencode 'audit <id>''). If the audit says not ready to close then the process is repeated but with the command 'opencode 'address the gaps identified in the audit for <id>'. If the audit reports the item is ready to be closed then wl finish-work is called, which results in a PR being raised.
