# Audit remaining mutating commands for the store-lock lost-update gap

## Problem statement

`wl sync` holds the per-store advisory file lock (`withFileLock` /
`getLockPathForJsonl`) for its whole fetch → merge → write-back → push
operation, but only a subset of mutating commands acquire that same lock around
their read-modify-write. The earlier fix (WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1) locked exactly
`wl update`, `wl comment add`, and `wl audit-set`. Every other DB-writing
command still performs an unlocked read-modify-write, so a `wl sync` that
overlaps one can be clobbered by the sync's stale snapshot — silently reverting
the mutation and, where applicable, dropping the accompanying comment. The gap
is already proven in production for `wl close` (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ: 3 of 53
release closes lost with a success exit code).

## Users

- **Agents / producers running parallel sessions** on a shared store.
  - *As an agent that closes, deletes, re-parents, or dependency-edits an item,
    I want my mutation to survive a concurrent `wl sync` so finished work is not
    silently reverted.*
  - *As a release operator, I want `wl close` to be durable so a release does
    not leave items stranded in `in_review`.*
- **Worklog tool maintainers** responsible for `sync`, `file-lock`, and the
  mutating commands.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every `wl` subcommand that writes to the store is enumerated in an audit
   table on this work item, each row classifying the command as already holding
   the store mutation lock or not, and naming the unlocked ones.
2. Every unlocked mutating command's read-modify-write is wrapped in
   `withStoreMutationLock` (or the equivalent `withFileLock` +
   `getLockPathForJsonl` pair), including side-effect paths — `wl close --force`
   (recursive descendants + audit waivers), `wl delete` (the soft delete and its
   own auto-sync), `wl dep add` / `wl dep rm`, `wl re-sort`, `wl create`,
   `wl reviewed`, `wl audit-waive` / `wl audit-unwaive`, `wl interview`, and
   `wl github import`.
3. A concurrency regression test proves, for each command class, that a mutation
   landing during a concurrent `wl sync` read-modify-write survives (item state
   and any comment intact), reusing the deterministic parked-`git fetch` harness
   in `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts`.
4. No regression: existing sync/sync serialisation, file-lock, and
   mutating-command tests pass; commands already correctly locked (`wl import`,
   `wl github push`, `wl sync`) are not double-locked in a way that deadlocks an
   internally-triggered auto-sync.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant docs-site entries (specifically the
   concurrency section of `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` and the locking
   section of `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`).
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing lock: `withStoreMutationLock(dataPath, fn)` in
  `src/mutation-lock.ts`. Do not introduce a second locking mechanism.
- `withFileLock` is reentrant per process, so a mutation that internally
  triggers `wl sync` (e.g. `wl delete`'s auto-sync) must not deadlock.
- Preserve all existing command semantics and output shapes; this is a
  durability fix, not a behaviour change.
- Destructive whole-store commands (`wl import`, `wl init`, `wl migrate`,
  `wl doctor migrate`) replace the store rather than mutate a record; they must
  hold the lock, but a lost-update *merge* regression test is not meaningful for
  them.
- Do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, or agent-infrastructure directories.

## Existing state

Audit performed during intake against `src/commands/*.ts` (read-modify-write
call sites and lock usage):

| Command | Writes | Store lock today |
|---|---|---|
| `wl sync` | workitems, comments, edges, audit, watermarks | ✅ holds the lock (owner) |
| `wl update` | workitems, audit_results, comments, parent demotion | ✅ `withStoreMutationLock` |
| `wl comment add` | comments | ✅ `withStoreMutationLock` |
| `wl audit-set` (`audit-result`) | audit_results | ✅ `withStoreMutationLock` |
| `wl import` | whole store | ✅ `withFileLock(getLockPathForJsonl)` |
| `wl github push` | comments, workitems, metadata | ✅ `withFileLock(getLockPathForJsonl)` |
| `wl close` | comments, workitems, audit waivers | ❌ **unlocked** — child WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ |
| `wl delete` | workitems (soft delete) + internal auto-sync | ❌ **unlocked** |
| `wl dep add` | dependency edges, workitems | ❌ **unlocked** |
| `wl dep rm` | dependency edges, workitems | ❌ **unlocked** |
| `wl re-sort` | workitems.sortIndex | ❌ **unlocked** |
| `wl create` | workitems, audit_results, parent demotion | ❌ **unlocked** |
| `wl reviewed` | workitems.needsProducerReview | ❌ **unlocked** |
| `wl audit-waive` / `wl audit-unwaive` | workitems.auditWaiver | ❌ **unlocked** |
| `wl interview` | workitems.needsProducerReview | ❌ **unlocked** |
| `wl github import` | workitems, comments, metadata | ❌ **unlocked** |
| `wl doctor <writing subcommands>` | workitems via `--apply` paths; `doctor migrate` whole store | ❌ **unlocked** (only its remote push path is locked) |
| `wl init` | whole store | ❌ **unlocked** |
| `wl migrate` | whole store | ❌ **unlocked** |

Evidence: `rg 'db\.(update|createComment|...)' src/commands/` plus a
per-command lock check; `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` already covers the
`wl update` + `wl comment add` path and is the harness to extend.

## Desired change

1. Complete the command inventory above (confirm no DB-writing command is
   missed) and record it on the work item.
2. Wrap each unlocked command's full read-modify-write — including recursive
   and side-effect paths — in `withStoreMutationLock`, matching the pattern in
   `src/commands/update.ts`.
3. For `wl delete`, take the lock across the delete loop (the auto-sync it
   triggers is reentrant and must not deadlock).
4. Add a concurrency regression test per command class to
   `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` (or a sibling suite) using the existing
   parked-`git fetch` shim, asserting the mutation survives.
5. Update the concurrency documentation to state the full set of locked
   mutating commands.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/mutation-lock.ts` — existing `withStoreMutationLock` helper to reuse.
- `src/file-lock.ts` — `withFileLock`, `getLockPathForJsonl`, reentrancy.
- `src/commands/close.ts` — wrap the close/descendant loop (child work item).
- `src/commands/delete.ts` — wrap the delete loop; verify auto-sync reentrancy.
- `src/commands/dep.ts` — wrap `dep add` / `dep rm`.
- `src/commands/re-sort.ts` — wrap `db.reSort`.
- `src/commands/create.ts` — wrap create + audit persistence + parent demotion.
- `src/commands/reviewed.ts` — wrap `db.update`.
- `src/commands/audit-waive.ts` — wrap waiver set/clear.
- `src/commands/interview.ts` — wrap the `db.update` write.
- `src/commands/github.ts` — wrap the `github import` action's writes.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — wrap writing `--apply` subcommands.
- `src/commands/import.ts` / `src/commands/init.ts` / `src/commands/migrate.ts` — confirm whole-store lock scope.
- `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` — concurrency regression tests.
- `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` — §9 Concurrency & existing protections.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — locking / concurrent-access description.

## Assumptions

- **Scope includes every DB-writing command**, not only the lifecycle writers
  named in the seed description (`close`, `dep`, `re-sort`, `github import/push`).
  The seed's acceptance says "enumerate every DB-writing command", so `create`,
  `reviewed`, `audit-waive`, `interview`, and writing `doctor` subcommands are in
  scope; whole-store commands (`import`, `init`, `migrate`, `doctor migrate`) are
  locked but exempt from the merge-regression test.
- **One child already exists** for the `wl close` instance
  (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ); it is the first command-class fix and its regression
  test is the template for the rest.
- **Decomposition** into per-command-class children is left to the plan step.
  This intake defines the umbrella only.
- The parent stays `bug` / `medium`; `wl close` remains the `high`-priority
  instance.

## Risks

- **Deadlock via reentrancy** — a mutation that internally triggers `wl sync`
  (notably `wl delete`'s auto-sync) must not self-deadlock. Mitigation:
  `withFileLock` is reentrant per process; add a test that exercises delete +
  auto-sync while the lock is held.
- **Over-broad lock scope** — holding the lock across GitHub network I/O or
  long recursive loops could stall other writers. Mitigation: keep the lock
  scoped to the local read-modify-write; confirm network calls stay outside or
  are bounded, as the existing `github push` path already does.
- **False confidence from exit code** — a command may still exit 0 while a lost
  update occurs; the regression tests must assert *persisted state*, not exit
  status.
- **Scope creep** — the audit may surface adjacent sync/merge defects (e.g.
  WL-0MQ057APG009I7IJ symptoms). Mitigation: record new findings as linked work
  items (`discovered-from:WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7`) rather than expanding this
  item's scope.
- **Destructive commands** — `wl init` / `wl migrate` / `doctor migrate`
  replace the store; locking them is still required but the merge-regression
  test does not apply. Mitigation: treat them as a separate, lower-risk class.

## Out of scope

- Redesigning the sync merge to be optimistic (e.g. `updatedAt` re-check); the
  chosen approach is the shared file lock.
- WAL/transaction redesign or read-cache invalidation hardening.
- Caller-side verification (the ship skill trusting `wl close`'s exit code) —
  tracked separately in SorraAgents SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5 / SA-0MUX8PYAY0008HFZ.

## Related work

- **WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1** – Fix lost-update race: `wl sync` clobbers concurrent
  mutating commands (completed). Precedent, pattern, and test harness.
- **WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ** – `wl close` lost-update: concurrent `wl sync`
  clobbers in-flight close (this item's child; concrete instance + evidence).
- **WL-0MQ057APG009I7IJ** – intermittent removal of recorded audits during
  `wl sync` (related sync-merge symptom).
- **WL-0MQQJDQ7M000X2L4** – `wl close` silently orphans children when no audit
  result exists (related close behaviour).
- Origin: **CG-0MUUFGXFX004O2X7** (TCE).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No blocking clarifying questions were required for this intake. The seed
  description plus repo inspection supplied a complete command inventory,
  precedent (WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1), and an existing child for the `wl close`
  instance.
- Assumption recorded above (scope = every DB-writing command) was derived from
  the seed's own acceptance wording ("enumerate every DB-writing command"), not
  invented. If the producer intends a narrower scope it can be corrected before
  planning.

## Related work (automated report)

# `wl close` lost-update: concurrent `wl sync` clobbers an in-flight close (item stays in_review)

Concrete instance of the store-lock lost-update gap tracked by WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7
(audit remaining mutating commands). The earlier fix (WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1) locked
`wl update`, `wl comment add`, and `wl audit-set` on the per-store file lock held by
`wl sync`; **`wl close` was not audited** and still performs an unlocked
read-modify-write.

## Problem

`wl close <id> --force` creates the close comment and sets
`status=completed`/`stage=done`, but does not hold the store mutation lock across that
read-modify-write. When a `wl sync` runs concurrently, its own load → merge → write-back
window can overwrite a `wl close` that commits inside it. The item reverts to
`completed`/`in_review`, its close comment is dropped, and `updatedAt` is left at its
pre-close value. The `wl close` process still exits 0 (`success: true`), so callers
believe the close happened.

## Evidence (ToneForge release v0.1.2, 2026-10-06)

The ship release close step (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`, which shells out to
`wl close --force --reason "Shipped in v0.1.2"`) reported closing 53/53 items, but only
**50** persisted as `completed`/`done`. Three were reported closed with a success exit
code yet remained `completed`/`in_review`, with no close comment and unchanged `updatedAt`:

| Item | Title | State after release |
|---|---|---|
| TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18 | Add CLI command to register new primitive recipes | completed/in_review, updatedAt 2026-10-06T21:11:16Z (== auditedAt) |
| TF-0MUUELBUD002OEQ8 | Repair main checkout node_modules symlink loop blocking npm/vitest | completed/in_review, updatedAt 2026-10-06T21:11:54Z |
| TF-0MMZIW9NQ09MV98G | Convert hard-coded recipes to ToneGraph configs | completed/in_review, updatedAt 2026-10-06T21:12:03Z |

All three had `auditResult.readyToClose === true` and `needsProducerReview === false`, and
re-running `wl close --force` on a **copy** of the store closed them cleanly — confirming a
transient lost update, not a data/content problem.

Timing (worklog data ref `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data`):

- Close loop wrote the 50 surviving items across 2026-10-06T21:33:33Z–21:33:52Z.
- A **delta** sync commit (`e993d47`) was created at **21:33:50Z — mid-loop**.
- The next full sync snapshot (`a0fc4c9`, 21:35:53Z) shows the three items still `in_review`
  with their close comments absent.

The three affected closes all committed inside the sync's load→write-back window; items
closed before or after it survived — the signature of an unlocked cross-process
read-modify-write, not a merge-preference issue (`wl sync` prefers the newer `updatedAt`,
so a committed, newer close would otherwise win).

## Desired behaviour

1. `wl close` (including the recursive/`--force` descendant loop) holds
   `withStoreMutationLock` across its whole read-modify-write, exactly as `wl update`,
   `wl comment add`, and `wl audit-set` now do.
2. A concurrency regression test reproduces the gap: a `wl close` interleaved with a
   `wl sync` load→write-back must leave the item `completed`/`done` with its close
   comment intact.
3. No behavioural change to close semantics otherwise; existing close tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl close` acquires the store mutation lock for the duration of the close (comment +
   status/stage update + any recursive descendant closes).
2. A regression test proves a close that lands during a concurrent `wl sync`
   read-modify-write is not lost (item remains `completed`/`done`, close comment present).
3. Existing `wl close` tests and the full suite pass.

## Notes

- Parent umbrella: WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7. Original lost-update fix: WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1.
- Related: WL-0MQ057APG009I7IJ (intermittent removal of recorded audits during `wl sync`),
  WL-0MQQJDQ7M000X2L4 (`wl close` silently orphans children when no audit result exists).
- The caller-side robustness gap (the ship skill trusting `wl close`'s exit code without
  verifying persisted state) is tracked separately in SorraAgents (SA-0MUX8PYAY0008HFZ,
  being refiled there as a ship-side verification guard).

# Herdr selection list: base the in-progress marker on work-item tab existence

## Problem statement

The "in progress" marker shown in the Herdr selection list is unreliable: it is
derived from the worklog `in-progress` status, which is maintained by the
hydrator — a self-healing loop that decides whether a claimed item is genuinely
being worked on by matching the item ID against live **pane titles**
(`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`). That pane-title matching predates the
one-tab-per-work-item convention: every interactive/downtime dispatch now places
its agent pane in a tab labelled with the **exact work-item ID**
(`getItemTabAnchor` / `findTabByLabel` in `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`).
Panes can be re-parented, renamed, truncated or multi-pane per tab, so pane-title
matching produces false negatives (→ wrong demotion, marker disappears while work
continues) and is needlessly complex.

## Users

- Herdr operator selecting the next work item from the selection list.
- Downtime dispatcher / plugin panes that rely on the hydrator to release stale
  `in-progress` claims so the item re-enters the dispatchable pool.

Example user stories:

- As a Herdr operator, I want the selection list's in-progress marker to reflect
  reality — an item is "being worked on" iff a tab named after its work-item ID
  exists in my workspace — so I can trust the list without opening tabs.
- As a dispatched agent, I want my claimed item left `in-progress` for as long as
  my work-item tab is open, so my claim is never released underneath me.
- As an operator, I want a stale claim (no work-item tab) released automatically
  and periodically so abandoned items return to the dispatchable pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An item is treated as actively worked **iff** a tab in the current workspace (`HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, or `herdr tab list --workspace <id>`) has a label **equal to** the work-item ID; a tab label that merely *contains* the ID does not count, and a pane title containing the ID no longer counts on its own. Verified by unit tests over a pure tab-matching helper.
- [ ] The hydrator's active detection is switched from `herdr pane list` + pane-title ID extraction to `herdr tab list --workspace <id>` + exact tab label match; the pane-matching seam/types (`HydratorPane`, `listActivePanes`, `collectPaneWorkItemIds`, `isActivePaneMatch`) are replaced by tab equivalents. Verified by code review + updated `hydrator.test.ts` (no `pane list` spawn asserted).
- [ ] Demotion rules are unchanged: a non-active item at stage `in_review` → `completed`/`in_review`; a non-active item with an active outbound blocker → `blocked`; otherwise → `open` (stage repaired to a compatible value). An item with a matching tab is never demoted. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] The signal is refreshed periodically from the selection list: the existing 30 s hydrate task (`HYDRATOR_INTERVAL_MS`) and the hidden→visible focus-resume hook both re-evaluate tab existence, so a closed work-item tab clears the marker within one cadence and an opened tab keeps it. Verified by existing scheduler/visibility tests plus a tab-based hydration test.
- [ ] Fail-open preserved: an unavailable/unparseable `herdr tab list` aborts the cycle without demoting, and tabs outside the current workspace never mark an item active. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries (notably the hydrator module header, `pane-title.ts` rationale comment and `herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` if it references pane-title matching).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the worklog status/stage vocabulary or the demotion outcome rules.
- Keep the bounded/responsive hydrator contract (per-step timeout, per-tick cap,
  stdio isolation, fail-open) unchanged; only the "which items are active" lookup
  changes.
- Reuse the existing tab listing/parsing (`listTabsInWorkspace`,
  `parseTabListOutput`, `findTabByLabel`) rather than adding a second parser.
- Retain exports still used elsewhere: `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`
  (`ship-guard.ts`) and `isActiveBlocker` (`stalled-work.ts`).
- No CLI or socket API change; `herdr tab list` is already used by the plugin.
- Write in UK English; follow the project's test/build conventions.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — fetches `wl list --status in-progress`,
  fetches `herdr pane list [--workspace <id>]`, collects work-item IDs from pane
  labels (`WORK_ITEM_ID_REGEX` over `pane.label`), and demotes items with no
  matching pane. Exposes pure helpers (`collectPaneWorkItemIds`,
  `isActivePaneMatch`, `decideDemotion`, `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — creates the hydrator runner with
  `workspaceId: process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, runs it every 30 s (`hydrate`
  task) and on hidden→visible focus-resume. The selection list's in-progress
  marker (`statusIcon(item.status)`) and Group N ordering (`status ===
  'in-progress'`) are driven by the worklog status this loop maintains.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — already lists/creates tabs labelled
  with the exact item ID: `listTabsInWorkspace`, `parseTabListOutput`,
  `findTabByLabel`, `getItemTabAnchor`.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — truncation helper exists specifically so
  the ID survives in pane titles for the hydrator; this rationale becomes obsolete
  for matching (the helper may remain for human-readable titles).

## Desired change

Replace the hydrator's pane-title-based "is this item active" signal with a
tab-label-based one:

1. Add a pure helper that, given the tabs of the current workspace, returns the
   set of work-item IDs whose tab label matches exactly (e.g.
   `collectTabWorkItemIds(tabs)` / `hasItemTab(itemId, tabs)`).
2. Change `HydratorDeps.listActivePanes` → `listTabs(workspaceId)` backed by
   `herdr tab list --workspace <id>` (reusing the shared parser), and update
   `runHydrationOnce` to use tab membership.
3. Keep `decideDemotion`, `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`,
   `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` and the bounded-run machinery intact.
4. Update tests and the module/doc comments to describe tab-based detection.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — replace pane matching with exact tab-label matching; rename seam/types/helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — reuse/export `listTabsInWorkspace` / `parseTabListOutput` / `findTabByLabel` for the hydrator's tab lookup.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — hydrator wiring (workspace id, cadence, focus-resume); update comments if needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — rewrite active-pane cases as active-tab cases; add exact-match, workspace-scope and fail-open cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.fixtures.ts` — replace `makeWorstCasePanes` with tab fixtures and update the exec router to answer `tab list`.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` — update to the tab-based deps.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — adjust/retire the "hydrator matches pane titles" rationale comment.
- `packages/herdr/shared/herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` — update if it documents pane-title matching for the hydrator.

## Related work

- WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI — Herdr hydrator: rescue `in_progress` work items with no active pane (parent of the pane-matching design).
- WL-0MTF5WO2Q008B8US — Hydrator: demote stale `in_progress` items (child, currently blocked).
- WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ / WL-0MUY1CYCB003DTKO / WL-0MUY1CYV6008BQWX — bounded/isolated hydrate steps (contract to preserve).
- WL-0MUKXFWLD006A8XI / WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL — item-ID tab anchor and interactive dispatch wiring (the tab-per-item convention this builds on).
- WL-0MUY1CS9E006ZLS0 — re-based Herdr in-progress UI behaviour on `status` (the marker this work makes reliable).
- WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 — per-row agent-status icon (separate, richer herdr agent-reporting signal; out of scope here).
